title: Standardize quota anchoring and billing-cycle alignment for reserved capacity
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: We have inconsistent quota reset semantics between hosted API (calendar/day aligned), reserved capacity (purchase-anchored), and rolling-window quotas used by some legacy internal products. This causes two customer-facing issues: 1) customers on reserved capacity see apparent 'lost' tokens when their monthly anchor doesn't match calendar months; 2) accounting edge cases cause duplicate billing around resets when requests land on the boundary under concurrent accounting paths. Goal: standardize how we anchor quota periods across deployment modes and ensure meter resets and billing alignment are correct, unambiguous, and backward-compatible for reserved capacity customers.
background: Incident log (2025-01-28): customer reported 12% token mismatch for January billing vs console exports. Investigation found that a subset of ingestion requests were accounted against a rolling-window cache on the edge, then re-counted by the central quota reconciler when the tenant migrated to reserved capacity mid-month. Similar issues reproduced in synthetic harness (see PR #846). Existing tickets ENG-8176 and ENG-9123 explored rolling-window reset options but left reserved-capacity anchoring decisions open.
acceptance_criteria: All reserved-capacity customers have a single, well-documented quota anchor (purchase start date) documented in Console and API
No double-counting observed when customers change capacity or cross reset boundaries (validated by replay test and production sampling)
Billing numbers (invoice tokens) reconcile to console usage within 0.1% for samples spanning reset boundaries
Migration plan exists and safely backfills any mismatches for affected customers with minimal service disruption
E2E tests cover: anchor computation, rolling-window fallback behavior, concurrent accounting paths, and edge-of-day DST/timezone transitions
tasks: Design doc: quota anchoring rules for hosted/dedicated/private (Confluence: /billing/quota-anchoring) - Owner: Daniel
Schema change: add 'quota_anchor_ts' to tenant metadata and make opt-in flag for legacy tenants - Backend
Quota reconciler: change reset computation to use tenant.quota_anchor_ts for reserved capacity, keep calendar resets for self-serve hosted - Backend
Edge cache: ensure transient rolling-window counters expose boundary-safe deltas (atomic flush protocol) - Edge team
Add telemetry: 'quota_reset_mismatch' metric and dashboard (Grafana) and alert for >0.5% drift per tenant
Integration tests: simulate mid-period purchase change and assert no lost/double-counted tokens
PR review and canary rollout: deploy to staging, then region us-west-prod with feature flag 'quota-anchor-v2'
Migration runbook and customer communications draft (CS/Acct)
design_decisions: Use purchase-start-date as the canonical anchor for reserved capacity instead of calendar-month to preserve contractual expectations
Introduce a tenant-level 'quota_anchor_ts' that is immutable for historical billing but can be migrated with an explicit migration step to avoid surprise changes
Keep rolling-window as an implementation detail for latency-sensitive counters, but require an atomic reconciliation handshake with central metering before any reset window crosses
Backfill strategy chosen: compute authoritative delta from request logs and apply correction as invoice credit where discrepancy > 0.2%
Timezones/DST: store anchors as UTC timestamps to avoid DST ambiguity and convert for display only in Console
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: migration may surface large historical mismatches for long-running tenants. Mitigation: run dry-run reconciliation and cap auto-credit to configurable threshold then require manual review
Risk: performance regression from extra reconciliation handshake. Mitigation: optimize handshake to be O(1) in the fast path and use batching for cross-tenant flushes
Risk: edge caches not updated atomically leading to transient double-counting. Mitigation: implement idempotent flush tokens and a short window tombstone for duplicates
testing_notes: Synthetic replay harness: ran 1M requests spanning anchor boundary — before fix drift=1.9%, after fix drift=0.02% (metrics attached)
Add unit tests for anchor computation (Leap year & DST cases)
E2E canary against 3 tenants with varying purchase anchors over 72 hours monitoring 'quota_reset_mismatch'
